elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence covers only professional liability (E&O) and cyber liability; no commercial general liability coverage or per-occurrence limit appears anywhere in the rendered language or elsewhere in the Agreement.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No CGL aggregate limit is stated; the insertion is limited to 'professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 and cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.'

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted E&O limit is 'not less than USD 1,000,000', which is the fallback amount and below the preferred USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Kubient processes visitor data under paragraph 9(b)(iii), so the condition applies, but the inserted cyber limit is 'not less than USD 2,000,000', below the preferred USD 5,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation covenant appears in the inserted paragraph or elsewhere; the rationale expressly declines to add it.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: The insertion contains no certificate-of-insurance delivery obligation.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: 'Kubient shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000...' — Kubient is the Vendor and the amount meets the floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: '...and cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.' — meets the fallback cyber floor for a vendor that collects and stores visitor data under 9(b)(iii).

reasons: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant anywhere (confirmed by the cited General Provisions in Section 14 and the deterministic 'insurance obligation present' check now keying only on the inserted text), so a concise insertion is the correct remedy for a 'missing' finding.
Fallback is complete: both atomic elements (E&O ≥ USD 1,000,000; cyber ≥ USD 2,000,000) appear in a single operative sentence imposing a maintenance obligation on Kubient, the Vendor.

Preferred is incomplete on four counts — no CGL per-occurrence or aggregate limits, E&O at 1M rather than 2M, cyber at 2M rather than 5M, no workers' compensation, and no certificates-on-request. These are not defects to repair given the fallback level was deliberately selected for this low-severity rule.

Minimality holds: the drafter omitted the model-language extras (at-own-expense, throughout-the-term-plus-one-year survival tail, certificates) that are not required by the chosen fallback checklist, deleted no existing words, and added nothing outside the two selected elements.

Intent is preserved: the insertion is appended as a free-standing covenant after Section 14(i), creates no dangling cross-reference or undefined term, and does not contradict the security obligations in 9(b)(iii) or any other allocation.

Drafting nit only (not a failure): the rationale describes the insertion as new subsection 14(j) but the rendered text carries no subsection letter — add the '(j)' label so the paragraph reads consistently with the lettered General Provisions and cannot be read as a continuation of 14(i).
